narrative.overview:
This system is a pre-flight briefing made visual: everything the pilot needs to know, nothing that doesn't belong. The design's job is confidence, not excitement. Every element earns its place the way a checklist item earns its place — by being necessary.

The system operates across two surfaces. The dark surface (marketing hero, customer portal) is the cockpit: deep navy panels layered in ascending lightness, instruments lit in cool-sky blue, no ambient noise. The light surface (marketing content sections) is the operations documentation: a blue-white ground with navy ink and precise borders — legible, structured, trusted.

The amber note (#f59e0b) is the one warm element in an otherwise cool system. It appears only on the primary booking CTA and footer hover. Its rarity is its meaning: when amber appears, something actionable is there.

This system explicitly rejects: legacy flight school websites (clip-art planes, 2010-era layouts, stock photo overload), and generic SaaS landing pages (gradient hero blobs, floating card shadows, Lottie animations, Inter-font-everything).
keyCharacteristics: Two-surface logic: dark cockpit (navy) and light documentation (blue-white)
Typography pairing: Newsreader serif for display authority, Manrope sans for operational clarity
One signal color (runway amber) — used sparingly on primary CTAs only
Depth via tonal layering (6-step navy scale) over hard shadows
Labels are always uppercase, widely tracked, small — aviation-instrument scale
The booking system and portal are the brand: design both surfaces to the same standard

rules.name: The Amber Scarcity Rule
rules.body: Runway amber (#f59e0b) appears on at most one element per screen. It is a signal, not a theme color. Never use it for decorative highlights, section accents, or icon fills.

rules.name: The One-Palette Rule
rules.body: Both surfaces draw from the same color family (navy-blue). Deep Ink (#0d1b3e) is Midnight Apron with the contrast flipped. The light surface is not a separate brand.

rules.name: The Uppercase Label Rule
rules.body: Any text that labels an action, status, or specification field is uppercase Manrope with at least 0.14em tracking. Never write a CTA in title case using a serif.

rules.name: The Serif-for-Authority Rule
rules.body: Newsreader is used only for Display and Headline levels. Do not use it for body, labels, navigation, or form elements.

rules.name: The Tonal-First Rule
rules.body: Add a tonal step before adding a shadow. If depth can be expressed by moving a panel from ops-panel to instrument-surround, do that. Shadows amplify; they don't replace structure.

rules.name: The Glow-Not-Drop Rule
rules.body: On dark surfaces, elevation reads as a blue atmospheric glow, not a downward-cast shadow. Hard shadows on dark navy backgrounds feel wrong.

dos: Do use Runway Amber (#f59e0b) exclusively for the primary booking/pricing CTA — one instance per screen
Do express depth on dark surfaces by stepping up the navy tonal ramp before reaching for a shadow
Do write all button labels, chip labels, and spec-table headers in uppercase Manrope with at least 0.14em tracking
Do use Newsreader only for Display (hero h1) and Headline (section h2) levels
Do pair the dot-grid overlay with the open-ceiling background on all marketing content zones
Do apply the ambient blue glow on dark-surface interactive cards at rest, and amplify on hover
Do keep GSAP scroll choreography to the marketing hero only; portal and booking flow use state transitions only
Do anchor every italic serif usage to a meaningful phrase within a display heading
donts: Don't use clip-art aircraft illustrations, stock photo montages, or 2010-era layout conventions
Don't use gradient hero blobs, floating card shadows on colored backgrounds, Lottie animations, or the SaaS startup aesthetic
Don't apply Runway Amber as a decorative accent, icon fill, or hover highlight outside of primary CTAs and footer links
Don't introduce hard box-shadow on dark-surface cards where a tonal step-up would achieve the same depth
Don't write CTA text in title case or sentence case — booking actions are always uppercase label type
Don't use Newsreader for navigation, form labels, body copy, or any text under 18px
Don't show pricing or eligibility behind a contact-for-rates gate — transparent pricing is a brand promise
Don't add choreographed motion to the customer portal or booking flow
Don't use more than two typefaces in this system
Don't introduce purple, teal, orange, or any hue outside the navy-to-sky-blue axis as an accent
